editorial:
Imagine being a good cop who does everything by the book, only to end up saving the life of a ruthless gang leader. That is exactly where you start with Dan. The movie kicks off with a gritty, high-energy feel that puts you right in the middle of Hong Kong's dangerous streets. You will see Dan try to do the right thing, but he soon gets dragged into a messy game of cat and mouse. He decides to team up with the betrayed gang boss to make the criminals fight each other, thinking he is being clever. However, the vibe shifts quickly from a police thriller to something much more unstable and scary as you realize Dan is not as sane as he seems.

What really makes this ride work is the wild twist that flips the whole story on its head. The acting is solid, and the action scenes hit hard, though some parts of the plot can feel a bit rushed. If you love movies that make you question what is real, you should definitely check this out. For the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the gritty details, or you can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. It is a great pick if you want something that keeps you guessing until the very end.
endingExplained: You find out that Dan is actually suffering from a split personality. The gang leader he thought he was helping was just a part of his own mind. He was the one committing the murders all along while thinking he was playing a clever game. In the end, Dan has to face the truth about his mental break. The movie wraps up with him realizing he became the very monster he was trying to lock up.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers with a big twist.
